title: Finite Q3 source-local graph-norm transfer and cutoff commutator stress
question: On an explicit low-occupation polynomial core, do the shifted source-local Q3 potential weights transfer through the full shifted Hamiltonian with finite graph and form constants, and does the associated commutator coefficient stay stable under volume, source translation and oscillator-cutoff stress?

model.graph: Q3 target edge, square face and 2x3 rectangular control with the registered seven-edge volume-6 subgraph
model.source_edge_weight: K_S=I+V_S+B_S-min(spec(V_S+B_S))I with B_S containing only bonds internal to S
model.polynomial_core: span of tensor Fock basis vectors with total occupation at most core_total_occupation

adversarial_review.check: The form constant, graph constant and commutator constant are computed separately; form domination is not substituted for an operator graph estimate.
The onsite source potential and internal source-edge potential are declared explicitly; bonds crossing the source boundary are not silently included in K_S.
Only the declared finite tensor Fock span with total occupation at most two is tested; no dense-domain or cutoff-removal claim is inferred.
Oscillator dimension is the finite cutoff stress variable; its sampled dependence is not identified with a continuum limit.
K_Lambda is shifted strictly positive before K_Lambda^{-1} and K_Lambda^{-1/2} are formed; no Gibbs inverse or modular floor is used.
The independent script rebuilds oscillator, graph, Hamiltonian, source weights and core rows without importing the primary script.
A cutoff commutator growth ratio is reported only for the declared V=2 support and dimensions; it is a route diagnostic, not an asymptotic no-go.
No common unbounded core, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion follows.

next_action: Use the finite graph constants as calibration only. Derive a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform analytic commutator/graph estimate on a declared Q3 core; if the cutoff coefficient cannot be bounded, retain the finite growth as route-local and move to a cancellation-aware history topology before any common-alpha promotion.

qft_interface.closed: Finite source-local Q3 potential and source-edge weights admit explicitly measured form, graph and commutator transfer constants on a low-occupation core across the declared volume, source and oscillator-cutoff grid.
qft_interface.open: The analytic uniform graph/commutator estimate, cutoff removal, common unbounded core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, all-shape exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite graph-norm transfer stress. It is neither a common-core theorem nor a thermodynamic QFT or Clay result.
no_overclaim: Finite matrix graph/form/commutator constants and a sampled cutoff trend do not prove source/volume/cutoff uniformity, a common dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
